  The notifier is deployed separately and cannot read the root flags.toml. Its flags are environment variables named `NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>` (upper snake case, value "1" to enable), read with `os.environ.get("NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>") == "1"`.
- [convention] Feature flags go through flags.is_on() (id: 01a10747-0a0e-7690-ab34-452dc8e4e7b1; source: shared/human)
  Read feature flags only with `flags.is_on("name")` from src/flags.py. Flag names are kebab-case and must be declared in flags.toml.
- [convention] Notifier email templates (id: 01a10747-b8b2-7a40-b326-b97300e40753; source: shared/human)
  Email templates live in services/notifier/templates/ as `<event>.mjml` and are compiled at build time. Every template needs a plain-text twin `<event>.txt` with the same variables, because some corporate mail gateways strip HTML. Template variables are snake_case.
- [hazard] Email provider: sandbox behaviour and limits (id: 01a10748-1413-7cb2-a4fc-3f5685a93649; source: shared/human)
  The notifier sends through the email provider's HTTP API (provider.send). Production credentials exist only in the deployed function's environment. For development there is a separate sandbox account whose key is in the dev secrets store; export it as MAIL_API_KEY. The sandbox has the same API and response shapes, but it is rate-limited to 2 messages per second and capped at 500 messages a day for the whole team, so do not loop over large fixtures. Bounces and complaints are simulated with magic addresses from the provider's docs. Important: the sandbox silently drops (answers 202, never delivers) every message whose recipient is not on the `@sink.acme.test` domain, so a test that asserts delivery must send to an address such as `receipts@sink.acme.test` and read it back from the sink inbox API.","hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit"}}

content.text:
The new receipt email is now behind a flag, and the old email stays the default. One gap: there's no new receipt template in the repo yet, so turning the flag on before that lands would break receipt sending.

**What changed** (`services/notifier/notifier/email.py`)
- `send_receipt` uses the `receipt_v2` template when `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_V2` is set to `"1"`. Otherwise it uses the existing `receipt` template.
- The notifier is deployed on its own and can't read the root `flags.toml`, so I didn't use `flags.is_on()`. Its flags are environment variables named `NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>`, and this follows that pattern.
- The flag is checked on every send. Any value other than `"1"` (for example `"true"`) leaves it off.

**Tests:** I added two tests to `tests/test_email.py`: one checks that the flag switches to the new template, and one checks that a value other than `"1"` doesn't. All 3 tests pass with `python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib tests`, run from `services/notifier`.

**Before you turn it on:**
- **The new template:** there's no `templates/` directory, and `render()` is still a stub that raises `NotImplementedError`. I named the template `receipt_v2` as a placeholder; rename it to match the real one. It needs `receipt_v2.mjml` plus a plain-text `receipt_v2.txt` using the variables `invoice_id` and `total_minor`. Copy changes are signed off by the Growth team in #growth-eng.
- **Rolling out gradually:** an environment variable is all-or-nothing for each deployment. You can roll out by environment or by deployment, but not by percentage of customers. For a percentage rollout I can add hashing on the invoice or customer id; tell me if you want that.

I haven't committed anything.
